entries.subject: Bulge
entries.finding: Salo et al. (2015), S4G Pipeline 4, table 7, NGC4321, model _bd: a Sérsic bulge (9.8% of the light, magnitude 11.424, half-light radius 9.58″ = 0.71 kpc, n = 0.639, axis ratio 0.795, PA 127.67°) and an exponential disc (90.2% of the light, scale length 61.14″ = 4.51 kpc, axis ratio 0.823, PA 158.22°, face-on central surface brightness 19.942, 19.73 as projected on the sky). Used as published; the half-light surface brightness the bake needs, 18.58 mag per square arcsecond, follows from the bulge's magnitude, radius, index and axis ratio. At the disc's 38.5° the bulge's axis ratio is one an oblate spheroid in the disc plane can show (intrinsic 0.22).

entries.subject: Stars in the picture
entries.finding: The picture was first cleaned only by the bake's pass over the Gaia foreground stars, which leaves the brightest stars, the faint ones Gaia cannot certify and those it reads as extended. The Nebula Lab's NOX removes them all and keeps the galaxy's arms and dust lanes; it also takes the galaxy's own compact knots and clusters, most visibly in M51, which was looked at and accepted on 2026-10-03; 3 of the 3 Gaia stars brighter than G 14 in the picture had a glow, filled out to at most 87 px (17″). The lab's isophote fill, made for ellipticals, left a dark notch on a spiral, so the glow is filled from the ring around it.

entries.subject: Catalogued objects as dots
entries.finding: 73 dots from 2 published tables: 62 planetary nebulae (Scheuermann et al. (2022), CDS J/MNRAS/511/6087, 1,049 rows in the file); 11 supernova remnants (Scheuermann et al. (2022), CDS J/MNRAS/511/6087, 1,049 rows in the file). Each dot is a catalogued object at its published sky position, placed where its sight line meets the disc. Its height above the disc is drawn from a 618 pc layer, the scale length over 7.3 ([Kregel et al. 2002](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0204154), [record](../../sources/kregel-2002-disc-flattening.json)); that height is not measured. Planetary nebulae near the centre can sit in the bulge, with the bulge's share of the fitted light there; that membership is drawn, not measured.

entries.subject: Ionised nebulae (Groves et al. 2023)
entries.finding: The table has rows for this galaxy, but CDS serves it per galaxy only through TAP, which answered with an error on 2026-10-03 (HTTP Error 503: Service Unavailable); the whole file is 43 MB. The dots follow when TAP answers.
